os_identity.description: Bootable Linux-based SARA Lite OS image that combines VNCE Office Suite access, integrated local development tools, embedded Lite pillars, NBS-based continuity, and an ADA-first operator cockpit.
requirements: Define the image identity as 'SARA Lite OS' rather than a generic desktop build.
Keep the image desktop-first, low-strain, operator-safe, and live-ISO capable.
Preserve CONTROL-only routing and SECURITY-first gating as non-negotiable platform invariants.
Support additive growth without breaking current local-safe behavior.
notes: The target identity is a SARA Lite OS workstation image, not only a remote VNCE node.
The design remains additive and staged for safer rollout.

hardware_targets.description: Primary deployment targets are x86_64 laptops and desktops, with future arm64 support once package and transport stability are verified.
requirements: Support x86_64 laptop hardware for the first production-ready image.
Support x86_64 desktops used as staging, development, or operator stations.
Treat arm64 support as a later-phase target once remote endpoint and package availability are confirmed.
Ensure UEFI boot compatibility for the initial deployment set.
dependencies: Supported graphics, input, and network stack
notes: Kernel-level acceleration remains optional and is not a phase-1 requirement.
Legacy BIOS support is optional only for fleets that still require it.

base_os_and_desktop.description: A Debian or Ubuntu LTS minimal base with XFCE preferred and MATE supported as a low-strain desktop shell.
requirements: Use Debian or Ubuntu LTS minimal as the rootfs base.
Install XFCE as the preferred desktop environment or MATE as the alternate profile.
Keep reduced-motion, large-text, and low-click defaults enabled from first boot.
Include NetworkManager and systemd-based startup for predictable node behavior.
Allow Wayland if stable, with X11 fallback where needed.
notes: The desktop should feel calm and readable rather than visually dense.
Voice-first hints and accessibility shortcuts should remain available.

office_suite_and_vnce_integration.description: The image acts as a VNCE remote node that connects to the final C# Office Suite server through CONTROL-mediated AMIP/VNCE intake and SECURITY-first validation.
requirements: Integrate a VNCE client shell for frame receive and input send.
Require envoy metadata with protocol='vnce', host, port, token, and caps including frame and input.
Route all Office-bound session start, resume, checkpoint, and close operations through CONTROL.
Ensure SECURITY validates attestation, lock bits, authority bits, and STABLES resume continuity before activation.
Treat the C# Office Suite listener, AMIP intake normalizer, shunt wrapper emitter, and audit bridge as required server-side boundary surfaces.
notes: Current workspace evidence did not confirm a complete VNCE server boundary in the visible C# code, so this remains a required integration surface.
Remote behavior should stay LAN-first and internet-strict until trust expansion is explicitly configured.

ide_and_devtools_layer.description: A local development layer with VSCodium, Geany, language servers, and build tools that supports development on the SARA Lite OS image without altering routing or trust authority.
requirements: Install VSCodium as the primary IDE with telemetry, settings sync, and remote tunnels disabled by default.
Install Geany as a lightweight fallback editor.
Bundle Python, C#, and shell language-server support from offline packages where possible.
Include git, gcc, g++, make, cmake, pkg-config, and core CLI utilities.
Include dotnet-sdk on x86_64 images if storage budget permits, or stage it as an optional offline package layer.
Register desktop entries and devtool init/audit services without creating a new authority plane.
notes: Developer tooling is allowed locally but does not imply trust bypass or remote listener approval.
Automatic remote tunnels and silent extension fetches remain blocked by default.

micro_sara_pillars.description: Embed a micro-SARA runtime consisting of CORE-Lite, CONTROL-Lite, SECURITY-Lite, MAMA-Lite, and SDK-Lite so the OS behaves as a true SARA Lite platform.
requirements: Embed CORE-Lite for AMIP envelope building, workflow_state attachment, machine_profile resolution, and deterministic flag support.
Embed CONTROL-Lite as the sole routing authority for AMIP normalization, AMIPI routing, VNCE route class handling, and byte-level shunt decode.
Embed SECURITY-Lite for VNCE attestation, lock and authority bit enforcement, STABLES resume continuity, quarantine handling, and audit logging.
Embed MAMA-Lite for ADA shaping, low-strain summaries, guided prompts, and readable status feedback.
Embed SDK-Lite for AMIPI adapter packaging, VNCE wrapping, remote endpoint fields, and reconnect metadata while remaining adapter-only.
notes: CORE-Lite builds but does not own final routing.
SDK-Lite stays wrapper-only and must remain subordinate to CONTROL-Lite and SECURITY-Lite.

nbs_lite_and_continuity.description: Use NBS-Lite as the local continuity, schema, map, diff, rebuild, and self-repair layer for forward-compatible SARA Lite OS operation.
requirements: Store schemas, maps, snapshots, and deltas under /var/lib/sara-lite/nbs/ with a read-only bootstrap mirror under /opt/sara-vnce/sara-lite/.
Capture continuity snapshots at boot completion, successful session start, resume success, approved config change, pre-update staging, and clean shutdown.
Keep last-known-good and current-working snapshots side by side.
Rebuild from trusted bootstrap config plus schemas, maps, snapshots, and signed deltas.
Use diff-based reconstruction and additive self-repair rather than blind overwrite.
notes: If repair confidence is low, the OS should enter held safe mode and request operator review.
Forward compatibility should preserve unknown but well-formed fields in a compatibility extension area.

amip_amipi_and_shunt_support.description: Provide first-class AMIP/AMIPI handling and byte-level shunt enforcement for VNCE and local SARA Lite routing behavior.
requirements: Support AMIP required fields including amip_version, mode, routing_intent, resource_budget, payload, machine_profile, and correlation_id.
Extend AMIP additively for source_pillar, target_pillar, deterministic, workflow_state, and transport_policy where needed.
Define or embed AMIPI support with amipi_version, backend_ami, target_ami_id, dispatch_id, result_status, and error_code support.
Enforce shunt header bits for SECURITY_GATE_FIRST intake, VALIDATE_GATE authority, envoy lane signaling, and lock-bit behavior.
Require UUID-safe correlation handling and strict session continuity for resume and reconnect flows.
Keep SDK packaging subordinate to CONTROL interpretation of the shunt header.
notes: Schema drift already exists between strict schema and live runtime behavior, so alignment work should remain additive and staged.
The updated shunt map is richer than current live enforcement and should be activated carefully to avoid regressions.

cockpit_and_ada_profile.description: A minimal ADA-friendly local cockpit provides a readable SARA Lite OS control surface without direct authority override.
requirements: Provide a single-window low-strain dashboard with large targets and reduced motion.
Show system health, workflow state, routing posture, trust state, continuity status, developer tools availability, and network environment.
Allow observational and request-based actions such as safe reconnect, held-state rebuild request, and diagnostics export.
Block direct route override, SECURITY bypass, remote tunnel activation, or blind deletion of continuity state.
Expose cockpit launch from the desktop panel once safe boot completes.
notes: The cockpit makes the image feel like a true SARA Lite OS rather than only a dev box.
Cockpit behavior remains observational or request-based, not directly authoritative.

network_and_trust_model.description: Use a LAN-first and internet-strict trust posture with SECURITY-first evaluation of host, token, environment, and resume continuity.
requirements: Treat local_only and trusted_local as the closest match to current behavior.
Enable LAN support only with explicit environment='lan', transport security, host allowlist, token validation, and STABLES-aware session handling.
Treat internet paths as strict, never auto-trusted, and dependent on explicit trust policy, reconnect nonce, timeout policy, and faster quarantine on mismatch.
Require device_identity, session_id, correlation_id, and envoy_instance_id continuity for resumed sessions.
Keep routing and activation blocked whenever trust evaluation fails.
notes: LAN-first staging is the recommended rollout posture.
Internet readiness should be considered a later controlled phase, not a default capability.

iso_and_bootloader_structure.description: The bootable ISO includes the Linux live image, SARA Lite runtime, devtools, policy files, and minimal bootloader adjustments for safe normal, recovery, and diagnostics modes.
requirements: Include UEFI boot assets such as BOOTX64.EFI and grubx64.efi.
Include rootfs.squashfs, kernel, and initramfs for the live environment.
Place SARA Lite runtime, schemas, maps, cockpit, and devtools under /opt/sara-vnce/ and /var/lib/sara-lite/.
Provide normal boot, safe recovery boot, and developer diagnostics boot entries.
Keep the SECURITY default-hold posture intact across all boot modes.
notes: IDE tooling is a userspace addition and does not require a trust-reducing boot path.
If Secure Boot is supported by the target fleet, signed kernel and initramfs are preferred.

systemd_and_service_graph.description: Use systemd to stage the safe boot flow, restore continuity, enable SARA Lite pillars, start the VNCE node, launch the cockpit, and optionally initialize devtools and update services.
requirements: Seed trusted local identity and bootstrap configuration through sara-lite-bootstrap.service.
Start SECURITY-Lite and establish the hold posture before VNCE session activation is possible.
Start NBS-Lite to restore schemas, maps, and last-known-good indexes.
Start CONTROL-Lite before enabling VNCE node behavior.
Start sara-vnce-node.service only under SECURITY and CONTROL governance.
Launch the cockpit after the platform reaches safe ready state.
Initialize devtools and update sync with separate units that remain subordinate to the same policy posture.
notes: Recommended sequence: bootstrap -> security -> nbs -> control -> vnce-node -> cockpit -> devtools.
Services that fail trust checks should stop in a held or degraded safe mode rather than forcing activation.

update_and_rebuild_flow.description: A signed delta-driven update and rebuild flow uses NBS-Lite to validate, stage, dry-run, and promote changes while protecting continuity and trust posture.
requirements: Accept signed update manifests, schema deltas, map deltas, and optional offline update bundles.
Stage all updates in NBS delta storage before promotion.
Run a dry-run reconstruction using trusted bootstrap config and current snapshots.
Promote the rebuilt state only if validation passes and routing/trust invariants remain intact.
Revert to last-known-good and log the issue in cockpit and audit output when validation fails.
Require reboot only when kernel, boot assets, or foundational runtime layers change.
notes: Background checks may look for manifest availability, but silent install is not allowed.
This flow is intended to support forward-compatible self-repair without weakening the safety posture.

acceptance_criteria.description: Checklist-style verification targets for calling the unified SARA Lite OS image ready for staged deployment.
requirements: The image boots successfully on target x86_64 hardware.
XFCE or MATE loads with ADA-friendly defaults intact.
The VNCE node can stage a session request without bypassing CONTROL or SECURITY.
Failed attestation results in held or quarantined behavior rather than unsafe activation.
VSCodium and Geany launch locally without requiring network registration.
Python, C#, and shell language-server support is available from local packages.
NBS-Lite can restore a last-known-good snapshot and perform a dry-run rebuild.
The cockpit displays health, trust, continuity, and tool availability clearly.
No default IDE or service component opens unsolicited remote tunnels or listeners.
All required service units start in the intended dependency order.
notes: Acceptance should be staged LAN-first before any stricter internet rollout is attempted.
The build is considered incomplete if it only works by relaxing SECURITY-first behavior.

safety_constraints.description: Platform safety rules that keep the unified SARA Lite OS within the intended routing, trust, accessibility, and rebuild boundaries.
requirements: CONTROL remains the only routing authority for all remote VNCE and local SARA flows.
SECURITY-first gating must occur before any remote display or input path becomes active.
SDK-Lite and IDE tools remain non-authoritative helpers and must not bypass CONTROL or SECURITY.
NBS-Lite rebuild and self-repair must not weaken trust policy or silently override verified safe state.
Cockpit actions stay observational or request-based and never directly override routing decisions.
ADA and low-strain defaults remain enabled in normal, recovery, diagnostics, and developer modes.
Unsigned or policy-mismatched updates must not be applied.
If trust, schema, shunt, or continuity checks fail, the image must enter held safe mode, quarantine, or local-only fallback rather than risky activation.
notes: LAN-first staging and internet-strict trust posture remain the expected operational model.
Rollback to last-known-good remains mandatory whenever an update or rebuild threatens routing or trust invariants.
